comparisons.peer_topic: Performance and Delinquency Status of Modified Loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Defaults on modified loans within 12 months were insignificant in 2024 and 2023; as of December 31, 2024, the $650 million in modified loans included $546 million current, $58 million 30-89 days past due, and $46 million greater than 90 days past due.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures report on defaults of modified loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty. However, Chase (C) reports zero defaults for its corporate loans, whereas Bank of America (BAC) reports insignificant defaults for its credit card and other consumer loans. BAC provides specific granularity on the aging of its modified loan portfolio, noting $46 million was greater than 90 days past due, while C provides no dollar amount for defaulted loans, stating only that none occurred.

sentences.text: No modified corporate loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty defaulted during the year ended December 31, 2024.
During 2024 and 2023, defaults of credit card and other consumer loans that had been modified within 12 months were insignificant.

At December 31, 2024, modified credit card and other consumer loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty over the last 12 months totaled $650 million, of which $546 million were current, $58 million were 30-89 days past due, and $46 million were greater than 90 days past due.

comparisons.peer_topic: Past Due Loans Modified Prior to Default
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, there were two commercial real estate loans held for investment with a total amortized cost of $56 million that defaulted during the year and had been modified in the 12-month period prior to default, whereas there were no such loans in 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the specific outcome of modified loans subsequently defaulting. In contrast to C's disclosure of zero defaults in modified corporate loans, Morgan Stanley (MS) reports that two commercial real estate loans with a total amortized cost of $56 million defaulted during the year after being modified in the prior 12 months. This highlights a material difference in default occurrence between the two firms for their respective modified loan categories.
